newsitem.title: USA: Waigel - monetary policy should not be abused.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - monetary policy should not be abused.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Sunday that low inflation in industrial countries did not mean that monetary policy was available as a tool to meet other goals.
"The industrial countries generally have inflation under control," he said in a speech to the Interim Committee of the International Monetary Fund.
"However we should not conclude from this that monetary policy may relax in its awareness or is available for other goals," he added.
Waigel added that price stability was an important prerequisite for long-term growth and stable employment.
"The later costs of fighting inflation are definitely higher than the potential short-term advantages of an excessively expansive monetary policy," he added.

There was every indication that prices would continue to remain stable in Europe, Waigel said, adding that the planned European Central Bank was being set up in a similar way to the independent German Bundesbank, with price stability as its main goal.
"In the opinion of the International Monetary Fund its independence (the European Central Bank's) is even greater (than that of the Bundesbank)," he said.
"The European Central Bank therefore fulfils all the preconditions needed for a stable European currency."
